title: Are there any communities of game artists who embrace AI-assisted workflows?
author: Trisect-
selftext:
I've been wondering whether there are any communities of artists interested in game development who are open to using AI rather than being strongly opposed to it.

Let's say some of us eventually find commercial success, like Slotbound, and start looking for people to collaborate with on future projects.

Personally, I would prefer to work with experienced artists who incorporate AI into their workflows, simply because of the faster workflow.

With enough time and effort, even someone without an artistic background can produce reasonably decent assets using AI. However, I think the strongest combination is an experienced artist with a good understanding of art direction, composition, and visual consistency who also knows how to use AI.

I see it similarly to programming. If I were hiring a developer today, I'd value their ability to solve problems, make architectural decisions, and effectively use AI tools rather than have them write code manually.

Are there any communities, Discord servers, or places where artists and indie game developers with this mindset can connect and potentially collaborate on future projects?

comments.author: imlo2
comments.body:
You probably won't find a much better forum of discussion than this Reddit group right now, and some AI-friendly Discords.  
  
There's for sure many isolated, quiet pockets of professionals who use AI-tools and have been doing so for a long time - I've myself been spending most of my spare time on gen AI etc. since GANs started to appear, studying and testing how to use the tech to benefit.  
  
But I know from experience that there's been quite bad initially slow and quiet meltdown already for years now in so-called professional circles where the supposedly "real" game development happens, as a big majority of people especially in the so-called creative side of things (artists, writers, designers) have been just quietly watching with dread and belittling AI for years, and then shifting to mocking it and when that didn't work, direct attacks. And that's divided people to different camps quite heavily. So no wonder people don't openly advertise that they are studying and testing how to use generative AI. For context, I've been developing games since mid 90s, worked for small and big companies, and own game dev small businesses for quite a few years too.

replies.author: Trisect-
replies.body: That's what I thought... someone on Twitter summarized this in a way that for many professionals, can't see the forest for the trees. For software developers coding was a tool to get the job done, AI is just a different kind of tool. I wait for the moment when creatives accept that the world is changing and they should use their experience, taste and knowledge to leverage AI for professional use. I believe truly in the end there will be explosion of work when it is more settled. There are so many niches when it comes to games, that a lot of people can look for success there.

replies.author: mysorethumbs
replies.body: I think the trick is finding experienced artists who embrace it. At my last studio, our CEO laid it out for us. AI is not going away and if you don't understand the tools in your discipline your future job prospects will be limited. I can confirm as I'm now looking for work, AI is listed in many more job posts from AAA studios. There are definitely exceptions, some larger indie studios have taken a stance against it and refuse any use of AI in workflow or even job application, which to me in the world of ATS systems in kinda crazy, but that's their right. Whether people like it or not AI is holding up the tech sector and the US economy and I don't see that changing anytime soon. Regarding artists, my old team members are split. Some are against it, and some embraced it. Those who embraced it found contract work quickly, for everyone, with the recent industry layoffs finding jobs has been hard, but I'd be surprised if the big name AAA studios don't introduce similar mandates to incorporate AI into their workflows. To be fair, its not always for the benefit of the game if devs who are inexperienced start using GenAI for asset creation. It can create alot more clean up work if youre not trained on AI prompting and verification passes. I feel like the push is more about C suite portfolios than anything else, but that's just my opinion.

replies.author: mysorethumbs
replies.body: One avenue to look for artists who embrace AI may be LinkedIn actually. I've seen many art tool and tech artists making things for artists that speedup the pipeline.

replies.author: starmakereden
replies.body: yup I agree. This reddit forum and their discord is the only one I know so far that are AI-friendly. I'm a designer so I can help with that department in case
